title: Mexican Economy Accelerated at the Start of the Third Quarter of 2026
author: Clara Zepeda
content:
_This article by[Clara
Zepeda](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Clara%20Zepeda) originally appeared
in the [September 24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/24/economia/economia-
mexicana-acelero-al-inicio-del-tercer-trimestre-de-2026-inegi), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. **Mexico 's economy grew 3.3 percent in real annual terms in
July 2026**, with trade and services as its main support, and a more visible
industry, the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) reported.

The Global Indicator of Economic Activity (IGAE), calculated by INEGI to track
the monthly performance of the Mexican economy, **showed an advance of 0.8
percent month-over-month in July** , after June's stagnation and the 0.3
percent drop last May.

By component, tertiary activities (trade and services) grew 1.2 percent and
secondary activities (industry) 0.5 percent month-over-month, while primary
activities (agriculture and livestock) contracted 1.1 percent.

At an annual rate, tertiary activities increased 4 percent and secondary
activities 2.4 percent. Primary activities fell 0.6 percent in seasonally
adjusted figures, used to make the figures more comparable.

INEGI detailed that, with original figures, without any statistical adjustment
for calendar effects, the country's economic activity advanced 3.4 percent
year-over-year, supported by 4 percent growth in services and 2.7 percent in
industry. The agricultural sector fell 1.1 percent.

**In the first seven months of the year, Mexico 's economy accumulated growth
of 1.5 percent** compared to the same period of 2025.

Services and agriculture rebounded 2 and 1.8 percent; meanwhile, industry
advanced 0.4 percent.

“The IGAE result was supported mainly by the rebound in tertiary activities
and by an improvement in secondary activities, which suggests a broader
recovery compared to the close of the previous quarter; however, performance
continued to be uneven across sectors, given the contraction in primary
activities,” explained Rosa Rubio, economic analyst at Monex.

She added that the cumulative January–July figures show a gradual improvement
in the pace of activity, in which **industry reversed the negative trajectory
observed since August 2024** , while services continued to be the main support
of growth.
